title.narrative: Strengthening systems for health and scaling up of interventions against TB and Malaria - Sierra Leone (01-Jan-2016-30-Jun-2018)

description.narrative: Sierra Leone, Multicomponent, Ministry of Health (MOH)This program has the following goals: By 2020, reduce malaria morbidity and mortality by at least 40% compared with 2015. To build functional and resilient national and district systems for health that deliver safe, efficient and high quality health care services that are accessible, equitable and affordable for all Sierra Leoneans. To reduce the burden of Tuberculosis in Sierra Leone in line with the National Strategic Plan, Millenium Development Goals and StopTB Partnership targets. The objectives of this program are: All suspected malaria cases should have access to confirmatory diagnosis.. To enroll and treat 20% (49) of diagnosed DR-TB patients on appropriate treatment by 2017.. All malaria cases to receive effective treatment.. Provide access to 100% of the population at risk with preventive measures by 2017.. To increase Case Notification Rate (CNR) of TB cases (all forms) from 201 cases per 100000 population in 2014 to 276 cases per 100,000 population by 2017.. To provide knowledge to the population such that at least 80% practice malaria prevention and treatment measures by 2018.. To increase treatment success rate of TB new bacteriologically confirmed cases from 87% in 2014 to 90% in 2017.. By 2020, at least 95% of health facilities report routinely on malaria program performance.. To close the Human Resources for Health gap at the PHU, hospital and DHMT levels.. To ensure that communities trust the health care system and access essential health services.. To test all TB diagnosed clients for HIV and increase the percentage of co- infected patients enrolled on ART/CPT from 68.1% in 2014 to 95% by December 2017.. To strengthen communities to effectively communicate and effectively send health alerts.
